articles.title: Dust: Pretraining Transformers Without Backpropagation
articles.summary: Dust perturbs activations independently at every token, so each token is a virtual population member and one forward pass evaluates them all in parallel, approximating backprop closely at large population sizes and even exceeding it in some settings. This hints that in a compute-rich regime, we might be able to surpass backprop. Dust is orders of magnitude more efficient than weight-space ES and is on the order of $10^3$ to $10^4$ times more efficient than a transformer implementation of EGGROLL, a state-of-the-art ES method, from 1M tokens up.
